A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same 45-page paper, Artificial Kuramoto Oscillatory Neurons, including Appendices A–G. Complete text extraction and rendered-page comparison establish that the body, equations, figures, tables and appendices are identical.

before.justification: v2 reports original AKOrN experiments on object discovery, Sudoku solving, robustness and calibration in Section 6, with additional experiments and ablations in Appendices A and D.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental results in Section 6 and Appendices A and D. Their unchanged status does not alter their qualification as original empirical results.

M1.justification: The Kuramoto updates, convolutional and attentive connectivity, readout modules, training objectives, up-tiling and energy-based voting procedures are identical.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic and natural-image object-discovery datasets, ImageNet and Tiny-ImageNet pretraining, Sudoku ID/OOD tasks, and CIFAR10 robustness and corruption scenarios.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in every corresponding main-text and appendix comparison, including ItrConv/ItrSA, object-discovery baselines, Sudoku solvers and robustness baselines.

E3.justification: Section 6 and Appendix C retain identical splits, sample counts, preprocessing, model configurations, training budgets, metrics and evaluation procedures, including test-time extensions and adversarial-attack settings.

E4.justification: Appendices A and D retain the same component ablations, rotating-dimension studies, positional-encoding comparisons, cluster-count sensitivity, energy-voting analyses and symmetric-connectivity tests. Failure examples and cluster visualizations are also unchanged.

E5.justification: Uncertainty reporting and seed information are identical, including means and standard deviations across three initialization seeds for object-discovery results and five for the Sudoku comparison in Table 3.

E6.justification: All numerical entries, plotted results and qualitative findings match, including main-text Tables 1–4 and appendix Tables 5–20. No result entries, rankings or trends were added, removed or corrected.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and derivations are identical, including the generalized Kuramoto dynamics, Appendix A.1's connection to the original model, and the Lyapunov proofs and propositions in Appendices F and G.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain identical claims about oscillatory neurons, object binding, reasoning, robustness and calibrated predictions.

C2.justification: Interpretations and limitations are unchanged, including the proposed energy-based explanation of calibration and Section 7's discussion of unit-norm constraints, feature presence and limitations for memory tasks.

D1.justification: Appendix C's implementation settings and up-tiling code, Appendix A.5's timing information, and the code/project access information are identical. Embedded link destinations also match.

R1.justification: Section 5, Appendix B and the bibliography are identical, preserving the same citations and positioning relative to synchrony-based models, slot-based approaches and energy-based networks.

P1.justification: The first-page marginal stamp changes from arXiv:2410.13821v2, 14 Feb 2025, to arXiv:2410.13821v3, 16 May 2025. All body wording, headings and section organization remain identical.

P2.justification: Figures, tables, captions and page layout are unchanged. Pages 2–45 render identically, as does the first-page body outside the updated marginal version/date stamp.

improvement.justification: v3 changes only the marginal arXiv version/date stamp. The scientific content, evidence, reproducibility information and presentation of the paper and appendices are otherwise identical, establishing no meaningful difference in overall quality.
